name: Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic
native: Українська Радянська Соціалістична Республіка (Ukrayinska Radianska Sotsialistychna Respublika)

predecessors.name: Ukrainian People's Republic
predecessors.text: Cliopatria's UNR shape of 1919 (522,688 km2); the infobox names the Ukrainian People's Republic as predecessor

predecessors.name: Russian Republic
predecessors.text: the Kharkiv-based Soviet government of December 1917

successors.name: Ukraine
successors.text: Ukraine of 1992, the republic of 1954-1991 without change of borders

ledger.x: 1917, 24-25 December: the Soviet government of Ukraine is founded at Kharkiv, rival of the Kiev-based Ukrainian People's Republic: "The government of the Ukrainian Soviet Republic was founded on 24-25 December 1917."
1918, January: Bolshevik forces advance on Kiev, taking "Yekaterinoslav (January 9), Aleksandrovsk (January 15), and Poltava (January 20)" after Kharkov (26 December 1917).
1918, 9 February: the Bolshevik forces "entered Kiev under Mikhail Muravyov's [command] on February 9"; on the same day the UNR signed the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk with the Central Powers.

1918, 1 March: the combined forces "retook Kiev on March 1", "pushing the Bolsheviks out of Right Bank Ukraine"; the counterpart is the German Empire as the lead of the Central Powers' force, with the UNR.
1918, spring: the rest of the Soviet-held land (Kharkov, Poltava, Yekaterinoslav, Aleksandrovsk) passes to the Central Powers.

1918, 28 November: the Provisional Workers' and Peasants' Government of Ukraine is created at Kursk, outside Ukraine, while the Central Powers and the UNR hold the country; the seat returns to Kharkiv in 1919.
1919, 3 January: "On January 3, the Red Army took Kharkov."
1919, January: "On January 20 the Soviet Army took Poltava" and "on January 26 Dybenko took Yekaterinoslav".
1919, 5 February: Kyiv "fell to the Red Army again on 5 February".

1919, 10 March: the Third All-Ukrainian Congress of Soviets at Kharkiv ratifies the constitution of the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic, the republic "itself" being proclaimed on this date; the state of December 1917 continues.
1919, early: "a new, swift Bolshevik offensive overran most of Eastern and central Ukraine in early 1919".

1919, May: the AFSR offensive forces the Red Southern Front back, and the Denikin page has Denikin's forces checking a major Red offensive in the Donbas and routing the Red armies in May; the pages give no day for the Donbas.
1919, 25 June: "On 25 June 1919, Denikin's Armed Forces of South Russia captured Kharkov, followed by Ekaterinoslav on 30 June."
1919, 30 June: Denikin's forces captured Kharkov on 25 June, "followed by Ekaterinoslav on 30 June".
1919, 31 July: "He took Poltava on July 31, Odesa on August 23, and Kyiv on August 31".
1919, 23 August: Denikin "took...

1919, 31 August: "... and Kyiv on August 31"; the Ukrainian-Soviet War page agrees ("on 31 August Anton Denikin's Volunteer Army established its positions in the city"); the Southern Front page puts the front's loss of Kiev between August and October.
1919, autumn: the remaining Ukrainian oblasts are inside South Russia's territory at its October 1919 peak.
1919, 24 November to 12 December: the Red Southern Front retakes Kharkov, Sumy, Belgorod and Stary Oskol.
1920, winter: "by 1920 all of Eastern and central Ukraine except Crimea was again in Bolshevik hands".
1920, 25 April: "The Kiev Expedition, in which 65,000 Polish and 15,000 Ukrainian soldiers took part, commenced on 25 April 1920"; Zhytomyr was captured on 26 April, Kiev entered on 7 May.
1920, 26 April: "Zhytomyr was captured on 26 April" by the Polish-Ukrainian forces.
1920, 7 May: "The combined Polish-Ukrainian forces under General Rydz-Smigly entered the city on 7 May."

1920, June: the Soviet counteroffensive (28 May; the 1st Cavalry Army broke through on 5 June and reached Zhytomyr and Berdychiv by 7 June) forces the Poles out: "After 10 June, Rydz-Smigly evacuated the 3rd Polish Army from Kiev.
1920, June: "In June 1920, Wrangel launched his last major offensive, the Northern Taurida Operation" and "his forces broke out of the Crimean bottleneck and captured a large territory to the north".
1920, 28 October to 3 November: the Red Southern Front's "counteroffensive in northern Taurida between 28 October and 3 November" captured Perekop, Henichesk, Melitopol and Chongar.

1921, 18 March: the Treaty of Riga ends the Polish-Soviet War; the border runs about 250 km east of the Curzon Line, Poland recognises Soviet Ukraine and Belarus and withdraws recognition from the Ukrainian People's Republic, and western Ukraine goes to Poland.

1922, 30 December: Ukraine joins the USSR "along with the Russian, Byelorussian and Transcaucasian republics" as a founding republic; it keeps its territory and becomes an internal unit of the Union (union-of-soviet-socialist-republics).

1924, 12 October: "The Moldavian Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic was established inside the Ukrainian SSR, on 12 October 1924" (8,288 km2 in 1939); the Transnistrian part lies outside the Natural Earth Ukraine drawn in the keyframes.
1934: the capital moves from Kharkiv to Kyiv.
1939, 17 September: the Soviet Union invades Poland from the east, sixteen days after Germany; Lwow surrenders to Soviet forces on 22 September.

1939, 28 September: the German-Soviet Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Demarcation gives the Soviet Union "almost all Polish territory east of the line of the rivers Pisa, Narew, Western Bug and San".

1939, November: the annexed Polish lands are appended "to the Ukrainian, Byelorussian and Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republics"; Ukraine receives Eastern Galicia and Volhynia (about 200,000 km2 for the three republics together; elections of 26 October 1939).
1940, 28 June: after Molotov's ultimatums of 26 and 27 June Romania accepts and the Red Army enters Bessarabia, Northern Bukovina and the Hertsa region.
1940, 2 August: the autonomous republic is dissolved; its westernmost 4,118 km2 go to the Moldavian SSR, and the page is silent on the rest.
1940, 2 August: the occupation ends as the territory is allotted: the Moldavian SSR "was established on the main part of the annexed territory".
1940, 2 August: the Ukrainian SSR receives Northern Bukovina, the Hertsa region, larger parts of Hotin and the Ismail and Cetatea Alba counties (Budjak).

1940, 2 August: the Moldavian SSR is formed from six Bessarabian counties and the westernmost part of the autonomous republic (about 4,118 km2), "effectively dissolving it"; the page is silent on the rest of the territory, which the infobox lists as Moldova and Ukraine today, so it is drawn as returning to the…

1941, June: "Immediately after the start of German-Soviet War in June 1941" the Germans enter; "On 29 June 1941 OUN members launched an uprising in Lviv" and the next day "after the entry of German troops" Stetsko proclaimed the Ukrainian state; "By 10 July 1941, German forces found themselves on distant approaches to…

1941, 26 July: Romanian and German troops complete the occupation of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina; Izmail and Chernivtsi oblasts are attached to Romania, Odesa and the surrounding area becomes the Transnistria Governorate.
1941, by October: "By October, the Germans had captured Kharkiv and Stalino."
1942, 27 July: "On 27 July 1942 last Soviet troops retreated from Shchotove in Luhansk Oblast, signifying the occupation of the whole territory of Soviet Ukraine by Nazi Germany."

1943, December 1942 to February 1943: "between December 1942 and February 1943 Soviet forces expelled German troops from easternmost parts of Ukraine up to the Mius river"; the page gives no month for Luhansk Oblast.

1943, 6 November: "in Autumn 1943 Soviet armies advanced to the Dnieper, and on 6 November entered Kyiv"; the page gives no dates for Kharkiv, the other Left Bank oblasts or Zaporizhzhya and Dnipropetrovsk (earlier and later in 1943).

1944, early: "In early 1944, the Soviet Union gradually took over the territory through the Uman-Botosani and Second Jassy-Kishinev offensives"; the Ukrainian SSR page has "In April armies of the 3rd Ukrainian Front took Odesa" (year implied by the context).
1944, by October: "the Germans were driven out of Ukraine between February 1943 and October 1944" and "by 28 October 1944 expelled German troops from Transcarpathia".
1945, 29 June: "Czechoslovakia officially agreed to transfer Carpathian Ruthenia to the Ukrainian SSR."

1954, 19 February: the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet decrees the transfer of the Crimean Oblast from the Russian SFSR to the Ukrainian SSR (RSFSR amendment 2 June, Ukrainian amendment 17 June 1954).
1991, 24 August: Ukraine declares independence on the dissolution of the Soviet Union; the republic of 603,700 km2 becomes Ukraine (referendum 1 December, recognition 26 December 1991).

wars.name: Polish-Soviet War
wars.outcome: Kiev Expedition of 25 April 1920 (Zhytomyr 26 April, Kiev 7 May), Soviet counteroffensive from 28 May and 5 June, the Poles leave Kiev after 10 June; armistice 12 October 1920 (in force 18 October); Treaty of Riga 18 March 1921 puts the border about 250 km…

wars.name: Soviet invasion of Poland
wars.outcome: Soviet annexation of Eastern Galicia and Volhynia in November 1939 after the invasion of 17 September; about 200,000 km2 for the three republics.

wars.name: Soviet occupation of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina
wars.outcome: Romania yields after the ultimatums of 26-27 June 1940; Ukraine receives Northern Bukovina, Hertsa, Hotin and the Budjak counties on 2 August.

wars.name: German occupation of Ukraine (Eastern Front, World War II)
wars.outcome: Germany invades on 22 June 1941 (Lviv entered 30 June), has Kharkiv and Stalino by October 1941 and all of Soviet Ukraine by 27 July 1942; the Red Army expels the Germans from the easternmost parts in December 1942-February 1943, enters Kyiv on 6 November…

certainty.note: Civil-war fronts; the Soviet government held a few cities.
Treaty and decree borders: Riga 1921, the 1939 demarcation, Romania 1940, Czechoslovakia 1945, the 1954 decree; the Crimea/Sevastopol detail is the exception.
